retail_intro: Retail finally gets to trade the long weekend, and its favourite story now has a scoreboard: Trump's Truth Social topped Apple's download chart and then parked users on a waitlist, a classic launch-day test in which curiosity is cheap and the first opening print decides whether early holders get paid.

retail.title: Digital World Acquisition / DWAC — top of the App Store, stuck in line
parts: Why Retail Is Here

Monday delivered what the DWAC crowd paid for, and what should worry it. Reuters reported that Truth Social topped downloads on Apple's App Store while many users were waitlisted [[n1610]], which moves the bull case from a promise to a scoreboard: a chart-topping app, the crowd reasons, has to be worth more than 84.32 USD, DWAC's last close on February 18 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). The emotional hook has shifted from anticipation to vindication. The BBC framed the launch as Trump, banned from Twitter, returning with a new platform [[n1626]], and Sky News called it a bid for a social media comeback [[n1608]], the comeback story retail loves most because it doubles as revenge on the doubters. With US exchanges shut for the holiday, none of it is in the price yet.
What Is Driving It

The launch was real but rough. Reuters reported the app hitting the Apple store [[n1603]]; on Monday Forbes described a glitchy start with thousands on a waitlist [[n1613]], Bloomberg said it showed errors on launch day [[n1623]] and CBS called it a slow rollout [[n1621]]. That fits Nunes's own target of full operation by the end of March, per The Guardian [[n1604]]. Celebrity onboarding is the other engine: Forbes reports Sean Hannity and Marjorie Taylor Greene joined as the public struggled to sign up [[n1618]]. The backdrop is less friendly. DWAC's 15.32% gain over 20 sessions came while the Nasdaq 100 slipped 2.97% to 14,009.54 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18), and the market it reopens into must price a war risk that turned concrete on Monday evening, when Putin said Russia must recognise Ukraine's breakaway regions, per Reuters [[n0218]], and, in the Atlantic Council's words, Russia ordered troops into Ukraine again [[n1137]].
The Social Signal

This time attention comes with a ranking: Reuters' report that Truth Social topped Apple's downloads while many users were waitlisted [[n1610]] is a direct read on curiosity rather than a proxy. The explainer wave followed. Newsweek published a guide to joining and creating an account on iOS [[n1614]], PCMag ran an all-you-need-to-know primer on the network [[n1629]] and Business Insider a reporter's first-person test of the app [[n1615]]. For DWAC holders the waitlist is double-edged. Scarcity can read as demand on social feeds, but every user stuck in line is a download that has not yet become an active account.
Historical Analog

The closest recent rhyme is Coinbase's Super Bowl moment. ADWEEK says QR codes made waves at the game [[n0080]], and it now reports the Martin CEO publicly calling out Coinbase over its QR ad [[n0883]]; Coinbase closed at 189.16 USD, 2.76% lower over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). Interest that floods an app is a marketing win, not automatically a stock win. The general mechanism is the download-chart trap: a launch ranking measures curiosity on day one, while valuation depends on how many of those users are still posting months later, which no Monday chart can show.
Smart Money View

The professional mood is far gloomier than the download chart. Business Insider reports elite Wall Street investors saying privately that the market really did hit peak stupid and faces a cataclysmic shift that many will not survive [[n0788]], and Reuters that Wall Street banks fear inflation, asset-price deflation and even recession [[n0099]], the regime in which story stocks without earnings are de-rated first. Critics of the product are blunt: The Conversation calls Truth Social an ethically dubious Twitter for the right [[n1628]], and The Independent reports a little-known British company with an identical logo threatening legal action [[n1627]]. The bull counter is network effects: an app that opens at the top of the store with Hannity and Greene aboard [[n1618]] has a ready-made audience.
When the Narrative Breaks

Tuesday's open is the verdict. The bulls need DWAC to hold above the pre-launch 84.32 USD; a slide through the 73.12 USD of January 21 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18) would erase the run-up and confirm a sell-the-news unwind. Watch the waitlist: if the glitchy start [[n1613]] stretches toward the end-of-March target [[n1604]], the scarcity story curdles into a capacity story, and the logo dispute is a small but concrete legal overhang [[n1627]]. The war gap matters more. Crypto, which trades around the clock and stayed open through Putin's address [[n1284]], fell on Monday, with Bitcoin down 3.53% to 37,075.28 USD and Solana down 8.56% (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2022-02-21), a hint that the first full US session may open risk-off and drag speculative tickers with it.

retail.title: Lockheed Martin / LMT — the war trade finally gets its trigger
parts: Why Retail Is Here

The war trade's logic is the simplest on the board, and the grimmest: if armies move, governments buy missiles and jets, so own the companies that build them. Monday evening supplied the trigger. Reuters reports Putin saying Russia must recognise Ukraine's breakaway regions [[n0218]], and the Atlantic Council writes that Russia just ordered troops into Ukraine again [[n1137]]. Lockheed Martin last closed at 386.46 USD, up 4.11% over 20 sessions, with Raytheon Technologies up 7.06% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18), while additional US F-15s are sent to Poland to bolster NATO's eastern flank (The National Interest) [[n1367]].
Where It Breaks

The awkward fact is that the trade has not worked while fear built: Lockheed fell 2.46% over five sessions and the ITA aerospace and defense ETF slipped 0.84% to 104.30 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18), while Rheinmetall dropped 2.70% to 93.84 EUR on Monday (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-21). Defense budgets move over years, not news cycles, so a Tuesday pop can fade as fast as it comes, and Beijing's renewed sanctions on Lockheed and Raytheon over Taiwan arms sales (Reuters) [[n0794]] show geopolitics cuts both ways. If LMT cannot hold a gain above 386.46 USD, the war trade is being sold, not bought.

retail.title: China Internet ETF / KWEB — the bargain Beijing keeps repricing
parts: Why Retail Is Here

The bargain hunter's case for Chinese tech is simple: the banks say buy, and Beijing's giants are outlasting the US platform retail just watched collapse. CNBC reported investment banks from Credit Suisse to Goldman Sachs saying it is time to buy Chinese stocks [[n0155]], and Business Insider that Tencent joined the world's ten most valuable companies as Meta slid on its stock rout [[n0561]]. Meta Platforms (FB) closed at 206.16 USD, down 32.00% over 20 sessions, while KWEB, the one-ticker China internet basket, closed at 35.60 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). The swap feels like contrarian common sense.
Where It Breaks

The discount exists for a reason Beijing keeps renewing. The WSJ reported China ordering cuts to food-delivery fees, sparking a tech selloff [[n0693]], and Bloomberg that the policy wiped $26 billion off Meituan's value [[n0694]]; KWEB fell 5.04% on February 18 and Alibaba's US shares 4.37% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). The slide carried into Monday in Hong Kong, where Tencent lost 5.23% to 423.03 HKD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-21). Reuters reports Washington put Tencent- and Alibaba-run sites on its notorious-markets list [[n0200]], and Caixin says Hillhouse ditched Alibaba [[n0324]]. If KWEB opens below 35.60 USD and keeps sliding, the bargain is a value trap.

retail.title: 3x Nasdaq 100 ETF / TQQQ — the YOLO dip-buy meets a war gap
parts: Why Retail Is Here

YOLO now has a strategy page: Yahoo Finance calls it the new investment strategy raking in millions for young investors, though it remains risky [[n0825]]. With Fortune asking how low tech stocks can fall [[n0803]], the YOLO version of buy-the-dip is TQQQ, which closed at 50.44 USD, down 3.39% on February 18 and 10.99% over 20 sessions, against a 1.14% fall for the unlevered QQQ (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). Three times the bounce feels like a shortcut back to even.
Where It Breaks

This time the dip arrives as a gap. TQQQ last traded before Putin's address, with the VIX at 27.75 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18), and Europe has since fallen, the DAX down 2.07% on Monday (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-21); a lower open hands holders roughly three times the index damage before they can react. AdvisorHub reports a popular broker-dealer charged over leveraged ETF sales that cost clients $2.3M [[n1587]].
